task: Run the R7-010 runtime clone evidence gate from an isolated Team C worktree at the reviewed compiler SHA.
observation: The same compiler binary SHA produced different explicit-copy helper and fact IDs when invoked with the fixture under the L7 worktree versus the Team C worktree. The runtime evidence test hashes the entire generated Rust file after removing runtime markers, so the Team C invocation failed the historical digest even though the changed Rust text consisted of source-root-derived helper/fact IDs and the runtime template lines were unchanged. Normalizing the two helper-name occurrences and one explicit-copy fact marker made the output digest identical across roots; marker/operator checks and live sidecar authority checks remained exact.
impact: The unnormalized file digest prevented an isolated worktree from running a runtime-only regression gate on the same compiler. Narrow normalization makes the gate usable across worktrees without accepting an unverified clone or weakening exact checker-fact joins.

resolution.summary: The gate normalizes only the exact-form helper/fact identifiers while retaining marker, operator, live fact-query and sidecar checks; independent review of this Team C test change is pending.
